references.text: A similar command to help a donkey that has fallen under its burden, even if it belongs to your enemy. Both texts emphasize the duty to help animals in distress.
The immediate context deals with taking care of lost animals and property belonging to your brother. The verse extends the principle to also include animals that have fallen.
A righteous man cares for the life of his animal. This principle of compassion toward animals reflects the command in Deuteronomy to help animals in distress.

Jesus refers to the practice of pulling out a donkey or an ox that has fallen into a well on the Sabbath, showing that the principle of helping animals in distress was also recognized in New Testament times.
Jesus mentions that one would lift up a sheep that had fallen into a pit on the Sabbath, which connects to the Old Testament command to help animals that have fallen.
